Item0000000053.description: Stores only the populated diagonals and performs band-aware elimination with reduced fill and operation count proportional to the bandwidth. Common in PDE discretizations where the bandwidth is modest relative to n.

Item0000000054.description: Factorizes a nonsingular matrix A into PA = LU with a permutation P, unit-lower L, and upper-triangular U. Once factored, multiple right-hand sides and determinants are efficient, and the factorization is more stable than naive Gauss-Jordan.

labels.en: LU decomposition with (partial) pivoting for solving Ax=b and computing determinants

Item0000000055.description: Builds an orthonormal Krylov basis via Arnoldi and chooses the iterate with minimal residual over the subspace; restarted and flexible variants control memory and cost. Robust and widely applicable with suitable preconditioning.
Item0000000055.label: Generalized Minimal Residual

descriptions.en: Builds an orthonormal Krylov basis via Arnoldi and chooses the iterate with minimal residual over the subspace; restarted and flexible variants control memory and cost. Robust and widely applicable with suitable preconditioning.

Item0000000057.description: Performs a forward sweep eliminating subdiagonal entries followed by back substitution, exploiting the tridiagonal pattern for linear-time work and storage. Stable for diagonally dominant or SPD problems; otherwise pivoting may be needed.
Item0000000057.label: Thomas algorithm (tridiagonal matrix algorithm) for O(n) solution of tridiagonal systems

descriptions.en: Performs a forward sweep eliminating subdiagonal entries followed by back substitution, exploiting the tridiagonal pattern for linear-time work and storage. Stable for diagonally dominant or SPD problems; otherwise pivoting may be needed.

labels.en: Thomas algorithm (tridiagonal matrix algorithm) for O(n) solution of tridiagonal systems

Item0000000058.description: Forward elimination transforms A to an upper-triangular U using row operations and (usually) partial pivoting; back-substitution then solves Ux=b. This is the workhorse of dense linear algebra and forms the basis for LU factorization used by LAPACK and most libraries.
Item0000000058.label: Classical Gaussian elimination with pivoting plus back-substitution for dense linear systems

labels.en: Classical Gaussian elimination with pivoting plus back-substitution for dense linear systems

Item0000000059.description: Row-reduction with both forward elimination and full back-elimination to produce RREF and, optionally, A^{-1} by augmenting with the identity. Robust pivoting strategies are essential; numerical stability is generally inferior to LU with partial pivoting for solving Ax=b. This method is pedagogically transparent but rarely used in production solvers for dense systems.
